notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, for issue 1293, 23 September 2026. Verdict: accept. The extraction is session cc-39fac3's (issue #1292).

SOURCE, WITH A LIMITATION I WANT ON THE RECORD. The paper is open access (CC BY 4.0) and the extraction records the published PDF's SHA-256 as f2231145...3e07. I could not re-verify that hash here: Springer's PDF endpoint returns a 3 KB JavaScript 'Client Challenge' page to every request I made, with a browser User-Agent, with an article-page referer, and with a cookie jar seeded from the landing page; Unpaywall lists only that same publisher URL and arXiv for this DOI, and the authors' pages return 404 for the obvious filenames. I therefore verified the published TEXT rather than the bytes, through a rendering proxy, and reconstructed the journal page map from the running heads - 91 marks running from p. 506 to p. 596, matching the stated 505-596. Every quotation below was checked against that text at the recorded page. Crossref's record of doi:10.1007/s00222-020-00957-8 carries no update, erratum or correction relation, re-checked independently.

MISTAKES. All 20 findings were checked at their locators and all 20 are confirmed. This is the most carefully recorded set of findings I have reviewed: every `printed` field is a real quotation, every `reason` carries either a counterexample or the internal contradiction that settles it, and the classifications are honest - twelve are marked as affecting nothing, and the four that affect a stated result really do.

Nine are settled by the paper against itself, and I report those as decisive: E3 (the first half of Lemma 3.12 works with gerbes in H^2_et(A, mu_r), as its own proof says, while the second half is stated with Br(P)[r]); E5 (the Hodge-Tate display one line above selects h^{p,q}, so Omega^q must be Omega^p); E6 (a sum over i whose summand is indexed by j, with the X-side exponents); E8 (Claim 4.2 asks for a 1-gauge form eta with |eta^{tensor r}| = q^m|omega|, and the display identifies eta^{tensor r}, not eta, with (dx_1 ^ ... ^ dx_n)^{tensor r}); E9 (the same gerbe alpha_2 on both sides of a duality); E10 (the preceding sentence gives the space a P_{i'}-torsor structure, the next calls the isomorphisms P_i-torsor isomorphisms); E11 (D is a line bundle on X and theta is O_X-linear, so E cannot live on S); E17 (a surjection from a group of order e is called an isomorphism without the target's order); E19 (the Bockstein connecting map runs the other way, and psi carries two indices everywhere else).

RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN BELIEVED. Seven of the counterexamples I rebuilt myself. E1: with q = 4, s_r = 4^{1/r} and s'_r = 4^{1/r}e^{2 pi i/r} are both compatible systems, s_2 = 2 and s'_2 = -2, and no element of Gal(Qbar/Q) carries 2 to -2 - so the relation of Definition 2.16(c) is not well defined at prime powers, though the density argument saves Theorems 2.18-2.19. E2: a continuous Q_ell-valued character lands in Z_ell^*, (Z_ell^*)^{ell^k} = mu_{ell-1}(1 + ell^{k+1}Z_ell), and the cyclotomic character's image contains 1 + ell^m, so no ell^k-th root exists for k >= m, and no finite etale extension helps. E3: for y^2 = x^3 - x over Q_5, |E(F_5)| = 8 with full rational 2-torsion, so E(Q_5)/2 and H^1(F,E)[2] have order 4 while H^1(F,E[2]) has order 16 by the local Euler characteristic formula. E4: the conic x^2+y^2+z^2 = 0 over R kills the quaternion class, so Br(K) -> Br(X)_K is not injective. E13: x^4 - 20x^2 + 50 over Q_5 has q(p^2-4q) = 50*200 = 100^2, so its Galois group is cyclic of order 4 with inertia of order 2 - a non-split extension, inside the paper's own standing hypotheses since mu_4 is in Q_5. E14: -1 is a square in Q_5, so reciprocity sends it to the identity, not to a generator of Gal(Q_5(sqrt 5)/Q_5). E18: c_2(T_{P^2}(-a)) = a^2 - 3a + 3 has no integer root, so P(T_{P^2}) -> P^2 has no section although End(T_{P^2}) is split.

ONE DISTINCTION I WOULD RECORD, on E20. The substantive slip is real: Lemma 2.7(c), equation (4), has H^1_et(k, Hom(Gamma, A)) as its subgroup, and the proof of Lemma 5.12 prints Hom(mu_e, mu_e), dropping the cohomological H^1_et(k_F, -). But the finding also asks for the central extension to be written for I rather than Gamma, and the paper writes the same stack both ways, as [Spec k_F/I] = [Spec k_L/Gamma]; in the second presentation an extension of Gamma is the right object. So that half is a choice of presentation, not an error. Either way the conclusion |H^2| = e^2 stands, as the finding says.
